title: fix(cron): prevent duplicate one-shot delivery after restart

commit.messageHeadline: fix(cron): prevent duplicate one-shot delivery after restart
fix(cron): include delivery migration in PR wrapper closure
fix(cron): reconcile restart tests and delivery execution
fix(cron): scope completion authority to background commits
fix(cron): retain synchronous webhook delivery authority

P-04 accepted storage decision — September 27, 2026.

This records the campaign lead’s explicit task approval, granted before implementation, for the reviewed durable delivery-attempt fence and its SQLite schema/content-version migration. The lead separately clarified that approval does not cover an OpenClaw release, package, or protocol version bump. This is a record of existing authority, not a new approval or a merge request.

- Owner: the existing shared SQLite cron occurrence receipt. Its canonical monotonic attempt fact distinguishes `not-started`, `started`, and legacy `unknown`; there is no sidecar store or second recovery owner.
- Accepted tradeoff: state schema 19 → 20 adds the receipt column. Legacy ambiguous interrupted one-shots remain disabled as Unknown, including jobs that may never have sent and jobs normally deleted after running. Proven never-started occurrences retain startup recovery. A crash between durable admission and transport handoff can hold an unsent job. Removing startup recovery globally was rejected because it breaks the documented never-started contract; volatile evidence cannot survive the recovery boundary.
- Lifecycle: the field inherits existing receipt retention and deletion. FIFO worker writes, exact receipt identity, current owner authority immediately before dispatch, integrity checks, and settlement remain required. The durable transition adds a worker transaction before delivery; repeated admission is monotonic and only the first transition changes the field.
- Upgrade/rollback: use existing migration, backup, deferred-publication, and rollback owners. Schema-19 readers refuse migrated state outside the existing updater-owned admission window. Restoring an old database loses newer receipt facts and cannot reconcile messages already sent after that backup. No new updater exception is authorized.
- Validation limits: the original four-case regression failed for both duplicate paths and preserved both never-started controls before implementation; focused migration/rollback/admission tests passed. The single published-driver run installed original head `e318c7aeb39a43863a3b0100301302dcd4b5af9f` and returned `ok`, then failed standalone Doctor on WhatsApp reload. It did not capture migrated receipt columns and is not current-head survivor acceptance. The lead explicitly prohibited additional updater/Testbox attempts in this continuation.

The approval covers the persistence and conservative recovery design above. It does not waive CI, independent review, upgrade-evidence limits, or authorize merge, queue, or automerge.
